Selection Index for Genomic Prediction Objects

Source: R/selIndex.R
selIndex.Rd

Combines per-environment GEBVs from a multivariate gpAim fit into a single selection index, allowing simultaneous optimisation across multiple environments. Three index types are supported: a direct weighted index, the Smith-Hazel optimal index, and the Pesek-Baker desired-gains index.

Usage

selIndex(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
selIndex(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gpAim'
selIndex(
  object,
  weights = NULL,
  desired = NULL,
  type = c("weighted", "smith-hazel", "desired-gains"),
  standardise = TRUE,
  prop.select = 0.1,
  threshold = NULL,
  selected = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "gpAim" object, as returned by gpAim. For univariate objects the index reduces to the GEBV ranking regardless of type.

...

Currently unused.

weights

Named numeric vector of economic weights, one per environment/trait level. Names must match the levels of the Trait factor used in gpAim (i.e. object$GP$trait.levels). Required for type = "weighted" and type = "smith-hazel". If NULL and type = "weighted", equal weights are used.

desired

Named numeric vector of desired genetic gains, one per environment/trait level. Names must match object$GP$trait.levels. Required for type = "desired-gains".

type

Character string specifying the index type. One of:

"weighted" (default)

Direct economic index \(I = \mathbf{b}'\mathbf{g}\), where \(\mathbf{b}\) equals the supplied weights (or equal weights if NULL).

"smith-hazel"

Smith-Hazel optimal index \(\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{P}^{-1}\mathbf{G}_a\mathbf{w}\), where \(\mathbf{P}\) is the empirical variance-covariance matrix of GEBVs across lines and \(\mathbf{G}_a\) is the genetic covariance matrix from the fitted model. Maximises the correlation between the index and the aggregate genotype \(H = \mathbf{w}'\mathbf{g}\).

"desired-gains"

Pesek-Baker desired-gains index \(\mathbf{b} \propto \mathbf{G}_a^{-1}\mathbf{d}\), where \(\mathbf{d}\) is the user-supplied vector of desired gains.

standardise

Logical. If TRUE (default), GEBVs are standardised to unit variance within each environment before combining, so that weights are applied on a common scale irrespective of environment-specific variance differences.

prop.select

Numeric proportion of lines to select. Used to compute the selection threshold when threshold = NULL and selected is not supplied. Default 0.10 (top 10%).

threshold

Numeric. Explicit selection threshold applied to the index. If between 0 and 1 exclusive, treated as a quantile of the index distribution. If outside (0, 1), treated as a raw index value. If NULL (default), prop.select is used. Ignored when selected is supplied.

selected

Optional character vector of line identifiers chosen by an external method (e.g. pedigree-based selection, phenotypic ranking, expert judgement). When supplied, prop.select and threshold are ignored for gain computation: $gain is computed from exactly these lines, and the selection index is still fitted with equal weights (or weights/desired if supplied) purely for context and display. All line IDs must be present in the gpAim object. Default NULL (index-based selection).

Value

An object of class c("selIndex", "list") containing:

$index

A data.frame with one row per line, sorted descending by Index. Columns: line identifier, one GEBV column per environment (MV only), Index, Rank.

$weights

The index weight vector \(\mathbf{b}\) actually used (named, one per environment for MV; length-one scalar for univariate).

$type

The index type string.

$standardise

Logical: whether GEBVs were standardised.

$trait.levels

Environment/trait level names (NULL for univariate).

$genetic.term

Line identifier column name.

$Ga

Genetic covariance matrix (NULL for univariate).

$Gcor

Genetic correlation matrix (NULL for univariate).

$gain

Named numeric vector (one entry per environment for multivariate; scalar for univariate) of expected genetic gains at the chosen selection threshold: \(\Delta G_j = \bar{g}_j^{\text{selected}} - \bar{g}_j^{\text{all}}\). Gains are on the original GEBV scale (not standardised).

$selected

Character vector of the selected line IDs when selected was supplied; NULL otherwise.

$thr

The index threshold value used to define the selected group; NA when selected was supplied externally.

$n.selected

Number of lines in the selected group.

$prop.select

The prop.select value passed at construction time.

$n.lines

Number of lines.

$n.environments

Number of environments (1 for univariate).

Details

Smith-Hazel index: The empirical variance-covariance matrix \(\mathbf{P}\) is estimated directly from the \(n \times t\) matrix of GEBVs (lines \(\times\) environments) after any standardisation. When \(\mathbf{P}\) is numerically singular (e.g. when the number of environments approaches the number of lines) a small ridge is added to the diagonal.

Desired-gains index: \(\mathbf{b}\) is scaled so that the expected gain in each environment is proportional to the corresponding entry of desired. The magnitude of \(\mathbf{b}\) is arbitrary (only the direction matters for ranking), so the weights are re-scaled to have unit L2 norm before indexing.

Univariate objects: When object$GP$Trait is NULL, all three index types reduce to ranking by GEBV. A message is issued and the "weighted" index is returned.

References

Smith H.F. (1936). A discriminant function for plant selection. Ann. Eugenics 7, 240–250.

Hazel L.N. (1943). The genetic basis for constructing selection indexes. Genetics 28, 476–490.

Pesek J. & Baker R.J. (1969). Desired improvement in relation to selection indices. Can. J. Plant Sci. 49, 803–804.

See also

print.selIndex, summary.selIndex, plot.selIndex, gpAim

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# After running multivariate gpAim with Trait = "Trial":
# Equal weights across all trials (default)
si <- selIndex(gp.mv)

# Economic weights: Trial 1 worth twice Trial 2
si <- selIndex(gp.mv, weights = c(Trial1 = 2, Trial2 = 1))

# Smith-Hazel optimal index
si <- selIndex(gp.mv, weights = c(Trial1 = 1, Trial2 = 1),
               type = "smith-hazel")

# Desired-gains index: want 0.5 units gain in Trial1, 0.3 in Trial2
si <- selIndex(gp.mv, desired = c(Trial1 = 0.5, Trial2 = 0.3),
               type = "desired-gains")

print(si)
summary(si)
plot(si)
plot(si, type = "biplot")
plot(si, type = "weights")
} # }
